name: Bluegill Marsh
summary: In western Wetlands, Bluegill Marsh is claimed by the hostile Bluegill tribe. Their huts and waterways are guarded by Gobbler, and travelers risk being surrounded in the shallows.

sections.title: A Swarming Hazard
sections.body: Bluegill murlocs crowd the muddy flats and reed beds of the western Wetlands. Their tribe has built crude camps in the stagnant water and claims the marsh as its own. They live and hunt in close-knit packs. Travelers and scouts from Menethil Harbor risk ambush from every direction when they wade into Bluegill territory, where the chieftain Gobbler prowls the shallows.

faq.answer: Bluegill Marsh is a boggy subzone in the western Wetlands. It is the main home and nesting ground of the aggressive Bluegill murlocs.
Gobbler, a powerful and vicious murloc, rules the Bluegill tribe. He watches over its clustered camps and strikes down land-walkers who enter the waters.

faq.q: Why is it dangerous to travel here alone?
aliases: why are there so many murlocs
faq.answer: Bluegill murlocs gather in bands of two or three around their huts and shorelines. Their numbers and the deep, slowing mud make it easy to overwhelm a lone traveler.

faq.q: Why do travelers venture into Bluegill Marsh?
faq.answer: Scouts and adventurers from nearby settlements such as Menethil Harbor venture into Bluegill Marsh to thin the aggressive murloc population and recover stolen goods from their camps.

angles.text: Near Menethil Harbor, the aggressive Bluegill murlocs threaten travelers and supply lines crossing the western Wetlands.
